name: HashiCorp, Inc. (an IBM company since 2025)
subcategory: infrastructure automation (Terraform, Vault, Consul, Nomad, Packer, Vagrant)
origin_detail: Founded in 2012 (San Francisco) by University of Washington classmates Mitchell Hashimoto and Armon Dadgar. Hashimoto had built Vagrant in his dorm room from 2010 and was already working on Packer; the pair had collaborated on UW research projects (the Seattle project, Cockpit).
openness_notes: Tools were released under OSI licences (MPL-2.0; Vagrant MIT) while revenue came from proprietary enterprise editions and the HCP cloud, so the company was open core (2). In August 2023 all core products moved to the Business Source License 1.1 (source-available, non-OSI), so current level 1; unchanged under IBM ownership.

license_history.note: August 2023, for Terraform, Vault and other core products; Terraform 1.5.7 was the last MPL release.

relicensing_events.fork: OpenTofu (Terraform fork from 1.5.7, accepted by the Linux Foundation 2023-09-20; CNCF Sandbox 2025-04-23) and OpenBao (Vault fork, started 2023-11-09 under LF Edge)
relicensing_events.fork_backer: OpenTofu: Spacelift, Harness, Gruntwork, env0, Scalr (founding sponsors); OpenBao: led by IBM developers via LF Edge
relicensing_events.outcome_note: OpenTofu passed 10M downloads by October 2026 and is a CNCF Sandbox project; adopters cited include Allianz and ExpressVPN. Commentators found no clear evidence the fork hurt HashiCorp's business. IBM, whose engineers led the OpenBao fork, then bought HashiCorp and kept the BSL.

exit_events.note: Priced 2021-12-08 at $80 (range $68-72), 15.3M shares, ~$1.22B gross proceeds; ~$14B market value on outstanding shares, ~$16B fully diluted. Last private round: $175M Series E at $5.1B (March 2020).

Announced April 2024; closed 2025-02-27 at $35/share cash (enterprise value $6.4B) after UK CMA and US FTC clearance; runs as a division of IBM Software, not Red Hat. Price was well under half the IPO-day value.

risk_events: 2023-08: Switch to BSL 1.1; OpenTofu and OpenBao forks under the Linux Foundation
2021-2024: Shares fell from the $80 IPO price; IBM paid $35/share
2025-02-27: Independent company ended; became an IBM Software division
2026-03-31: Legacy HCP Terraform Free plan ended (replaced by a 500-resource free tier)
robustness: Now inside IBM, so financially secure, but product direction is set by one corporate owner and licences remain BSL. The community has two foundation-governed exits (OpenTofu in CNCF; OpenBao in LF Edge). Terraform development continues (1.17.x, October 2026) and is being folded into IBM's security and automation stack.
physical_science_relevance: Terraform/OpenTofu are widely used to provision cloud and HPC research infrastructure reproducibly.
openness_effect_assessment: MPL-licensed tools made Terraform the de facto infrastructure-as-code standard and supported a ~$14B IPO in 2021. The 2023 BSL switch was followed by forks that now have foundation homes and meaningful downloads, but there is little evidence it dented HashiCorp's revenue. Closing did not protect the company's valuation: it sold to IBM at $6.4B, less than half its IPO value.
key_takeaway: HashiCorp is the case where relicensing came late in the company's life and preceded a sale. The BSL change likely made HashiCorp a cleaner asset for an acquirer, and IBM bought it within about 18 months, even though IBM engineers had led the open Vault fork. The open-source community kept its own copy of Terraform (OpenTofu, now in CNCF), so the open standard survives outside the vendor.
